lines.text: Amazon released a free copy of AWS that runs on your laptop, and AI agents wrote all of it.
It began as a three-line prompt: write tests, pass them on real AWS, then build a copy that passes the same tests.
lines.title: How it started

lines.text: Three teams of agents work together. One keeps the tests, one finds problems, and one fixes them.
lines.title: Three agent teams

lines.text: Every fix must pass a merge gate of checks before it joins the code.
lines.title: The merge gate

lines.text: Early outside tests saw about 60 to 70 percent of checks pass for DynamoDB, S3 and SQS, but only about 20 percent for CloudFormation.
lines.title: How close is it?

lines.text: It does not check security permissions the way real AWS does.
lines.title: Know the limit

lines.text: Use it for fast, free testing. Test security on real AWS before you launch.
lines.title: Takeaways
